walkthrough: Identify the horizontal scale: each division represents $5.0\text{ ms}$, so the period is $T = \text{divisions per cycle} \times 5.0\text{ ms div}^{-1}$.
Reduce reading error by measuring several cycles: the screen shows about $3.5$ complete cycles occupying about $10$ divisions in width.
Calculate the time for these cycles: $10 \times 5.0\text{ ms} = 50\text{ ms}$.
Find one period: $T = 50\text{ ms} / 3.5 \approx 14.3\text{ ms} = 14.3 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$.
The closest best estimate is $71\text{ Hz}$. This is option B.
